name: Pythagorean number theory and musical ratios
summary: Whole-number ratios behind consonant string lengths supported a programme of studying even, odd, triangular and perfect numbers as objects in themselves.

name: Eudoxus homocentric spheres
summary: Planetary motion was modelled by nested rotating spheres whose combined motion produces the observed paths.

name: Eudoxus: theory of proportion and exhaustion
summary: Eudoxus gave a theory of ratios for incommensurables and the exhaustion method, a precursor of integration.

name: Euclid Books VII-IX: arithmetic as a deductive theory
summary: Divisibility, the Euclidean algorithm and geometric progressions of integers were developed as a self-contained deductive body.

name: Pingala: combinatorics of poetic meters
summary: Counting patterns of long and short syllables yielded binomial-type identities and a binary-like device; Halayudha later described the triangle.

name: Archimedes' mechanical method for areas and volumes
summary: Balancing figures on a lever (centres of gravity) is used to discover area and volume results later proved by exhaustion.

name: Babylonian astronomical parameters enter Greek astronomy
summary: Greek geometric lunar models were tested and calibrated against Babylonian period parameters and eclipse records.

name: Trigonometry from astronomy: Hipparchus and chord tables
summary: Hipparchus compiled chord tables for astronomical computation, and later Menelaus, Indian astronomers and Pitiscus developed spherical trigonometry, sine tables and the name.

name: Menelaus: spherical trigonometry
summary: Menelaus' Sphaerica gave theorems on spherical triangles.

name: Ptolemy's Almagest
summary: Ptolemy extended chord tables with sum, difference and half-angle formulas for astronomical computation.
